# Transcribe Video

- Route: `/tools/transcribe-video`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `ai`
- Slug: `transcribe-video`

## Summary

Pull the spoken words out of a video or audio file as WebVTT or SRT captions, plain text, or timestamped JSON. (AI tools)

## Details

Transcribe Video takes an MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV or a plain audio file, separates the audio track, and runs it through Whisper on a GPU server we operate. You choose the shape of the result before you upload: a WebVTT or SRT caption file with cue timings, a plain text file with just the words, or a JSON document with every segment and its start and end time to the millisecond. The language is detected automatically, or you can type a two-letter code to pin it.
### What it does
- Decodes the audio track with ffmpeg into a 16 kHz mono WAV, the sample rate Whisper expects, and deletes that intermediate when the job finishes.
- Runs whisper-ctranslate2 with the medium Whisper model in float16 on our GPU, with voice-activity filtering switched on so silence and long stretches of music are skipped.
- Writes one file named transcript.vtt, transcript.srt, transcript.txt or transcript.json, depending on the format you picked.
- Detects the spoken language from the audio itself; a language code you type in the form overrides detection for short or mixed clips.
- Reports honestly when there is nothing to transcribe: a video with no audio stream, or audio with no recognizable speech, still completes with a short message instead of an empty file.
### How to use it
1. Upload video or audio: MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, AVI, or an audio file such as MP3, WAV, M4A or FLAC.
2. Pick a format: VTT or SRT for captions, TXT for a readable transcript, JSON for timestamps you can process.
3. ffmpeg extracts the audio: The track is converted to 16 kHz mono PCM; the video frames are never decoded.
4. Whisper transcribes on our GPU: The job waits for a free GPU slot, then the medium model runs over the whole file in one pass.
5. Download the transcript: The file appears with the job and can be downloaded as long as the job is kept.
### Technical details
- The exact extraction command is ffmpeg -vn -acodec pcm_s16le -ar 16000 -ac 1, so a stereo 48 kHz track is folded to mono and resampled before Whisper sees it. That intermediate costs 32 KB per second (about 1.9 MB per minute) of disk while the job runs and is removed afterwards.
- whisper-ctranslate2 is launched with --model medium --device cuda --compute_type float16 --vad_filter True and --output_format json; the API parses that JSON and renders your chosen format itself. The model is a server setting (WHISPER_CT2_MODEL), so medium is the default, not a promise.
- VTT output starts with the WEBVTT header and numbers each cue; timestamps are HH:MM:SS.mmm. SRT is the same cue list with comma millisecond separators. A segment whose end equals its start is given half a second so players still display it.
- JSON output contains language, hasAudio, hasSpeech, transcript, durationSeconds and a segments array of {id, start, end, text} with times rounded to the millisecond. There are no per-word timings and no confidence scores in this output.
- Only one Whisper process runs at a time by default (WHISPER_GPU_CONCURRENCY=1), and the GPU scheduler checks free VRAM before starting; the medium model in float16 needs about 3.5 GB plus a 512 MB margin. If the card is busy your job waits in the queue rather than failing.
- With the VAD filter on, a file that is all music or very faint speech can come back with "Audio was detected but no recognizable speech was found." That message is written into the transcript file so the download is never empty.
### When not to use it
Do not use this when you need per-word timings, speaker labels, or confidence scores: the output has none of those, only segment-level timestamps. It is also the wrong tool for a file whose audio is music with no speech, since the voice-activity filter will skip it and you will get a short message instead of lyrics. If you only need to listen to the file, or you want captions translated into another language, you are after a different step. Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block.
### Use cases
- Captions for a published video: Export VTT for HTML video and most web players, or SRT for editing suites and TV-style subtitle workflows.
- Meeting and interview notes: Take the TXT output into a document and edit from there instead of typing from scratch.
- Indexing a recording archive: Use the JSON segments to build a search index that points at the exact second a word was spoken.
- A first draft of an article: Transcribe a talk or screencast, then rewrite the plain text into prose.
### FAQ
Q: Which caption format should I pick, VTT or SRT?
A: VTT if the captions are for the web (HTML video, most players) and SRT if they are going into a video editor or a broadcast-style workflow. Both contain the same cues; only the header and the millisecond separator differ, a period in VTT and a comma in SRT.
Q: Does the JSON transcript include confidence scores or word timings?
A: No. Each segment has an id, a start and end time in seconds (rounded to the millisecond) and its text. The file also records the detected language, the duration and whether speech was found, but there are no per-word timings and no probabilities.
Q: How long a file can I transcribe?
A: Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block. The form shows the limits that apply to you, and /pricing lists the current numbers.
Q: Why did I get "no recognizable speech was found"?
A: Whisper runs with voice-activity detection switched on, so a file that is music, ambient sound, silence or very faint speech can be trimmed to nothing. The message is written into the transcript file itself so the download still works. Re-record louder or trim to the spoken part and try again.
Q: Can I force the language instead of letting it detect?
A: Yes. Type a two-letter language code such as en, de or es in the language field and Whisper will transcribe in that language. Leave it blank for automatic detection, which works well on clips longer than a few seconds.
Q: Does transcription use my AI allowance?
A: Yes. Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block. The AI allowance is its own counter, so transcribing never uses up the everyday allowance for conversions. A job that fails refunds the unit.
Q: What model is used, and can I pick a bigger one?
A: The service runs whisper-ctranslate2 with the medium model in float16 on a CUDA GPU by default. There is no model picker in the form; the model is set on the server, so very fast or very large variants are not something you can request per job.
